solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tour base developed on largely modern resort

indicators.note: something developed has been worked up into a new form, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged
largely means most but not all, so the following word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
modern means new

explanation.surface: A holiday firm sets up its base of operations in a fairly modern seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give EASTBOUR, and most of NEW gives NE to finish EASTBOURNE, a seaside town on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastbourne is a well-known English seaside holiday town, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Free can is put in front of hotel

blocks.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is lav
taken as written
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A complimentary tin is placed at a hotel's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a tin; it is slang for a toilet. 'Free' here is the adjective meaning generous, not costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Free in the sense of generous or unstinting: a lavish host gives without holding back.

clue.text: Rather poor creed I'm reworking? Nothing in it

indicators.note: reworking something remakes it in a new shape, so those letters are rearranged
the zero goes inside the rearranged result, which is what 'it' points back to

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone revising their beliefs finds them rather thin, with nothing at their core.
explanation.walkthrough: CREED I'M rearranges to MEDICRE, and O goes inside after MEDI to make MEDIOCRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means of only middling quality, not good, which is what rather poor describes.

clue.text: Titled figures rose around theatre's entrance for actress

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the word from the bottom up
an entrance is the way in, so only the opening letter is taken
the turned word wraps round the single letter

blocks.note: peers are lords, people with titles
first letter of theatre

explanation.surface: The nobility stood to applaud an actress as she came into the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: PEERS read upwards is SREEP, and T goes in after the S to give STREEP, as in Meryl Streep.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is a celebrated American film star, an instance of a female performer.

clue.text: GP soon in after surgery? That's being nosy

indicators.note: surgery cuts and rearranges, so the preceding words are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor drops by soon after an operation, which the patient thinks rather intrusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surgery' looks like the GP's consulting room, but 'after surgery' tells you the letters have been operated on.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooping is prying into other people's affairs, exactly the behaviour of someone being nosy.

clue.text: School missing old Australian, source of fiery outpourings?

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the school name goes without the letter for old

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school
O is the standard abbreviation for old
A is an abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: A school that has lost an elderly Australian teacher, perhaps one known for angry outbursts.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON without O leaves ETN, then A is added. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, which pours out lava, so it is a source of fiery outflows.

clue.text: Daily journalist reflected about a pretence

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the journalist's abbreviation is turned round
about means surrounding, so the pieces before it wrap round the following letter

blocks.note: a daily or char is a cleaning lady who comes in each day
ED, editor, is the standard crossword journalist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer on a daily newspaper looks back on some sham or deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper, but in Britain a daily is a cleaning lady who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, an act put on that everyone can see through.

clue.text: I arrange steps?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who sets out a flight of stairs or stepping stones
setter's reading: the person who devises the dance moves for a ballet or show

explanation.walkthrough: Steps suggests stairs or a plan of action; here they are dance steps, and the person speaking creates the routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A choreographer composes and arranges the sequence of movements dancers perform.

clue.text: Challenger, perhaps, put back prize garment

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the word for a prize is read right to left

blocks.note: the Challenger is a British army battle tank; perhaps marks an example
a pot is a trophy or prize, as in a sports cup

explanation.surface: A contender in a competition returns the trophy they had won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Challenger' looks like a sporting contender; it is the name of a British army tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless knitted pullover, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Reasonable for head to include speech giving out answer

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so the word for head goes round the speech
giving out means handing over and so losing, so the speech word drops a letter

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
pate is an old word for the head
an oration is a formal speech
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A sensible headteacher works an answer into the address they give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For head' reads as a headteacher, but 'for' and 'head' are separate pieces; pate is an old word for the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportionate means in due measure, not excessive, which is one sense of reasonable.

clue.text: Note inch I shifted in a vulnerable position

indicators.note: shifted letters have been moved about, so these words come out in another order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Edging an inch over puts the speaker in a precarious spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pictures someone on frozen water that may crack, meaning at risk of disaster.

clue.text: NZ region given name in middle of book

indicators.note: in places the word for name inside the selected letters
middle of keeps only the central letters of the following word

blocks.note: the two central letters of book
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A New Zealand district gets its name from a passage halfway through a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is an administrative region in the south of New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Time hard to manage in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the combined letters are read right to left

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: A period that is difficult to get through when you are falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: H plus COPE gives HCOPE, which read backwards is EPOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period or era, a sense of time as in 'in our time'.

clue.text: Island firm touring Channel Islands for composition

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so the word for firm encloses the abbreviation

blocks.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
CO is short for company
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: An island-based business on a trip round Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British crown dependencies off Normandy, including Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a lively, free-form piece of music, so it is a musical work.

clue.text: Fruit and a roll supplied by place in crescent

indicators.note: in tells us the preceding pieces sit inside the abbreviation for crescent

blocks.note: taken as written
a bap is a soft bread roll
PL is the street-name abbreviation for place
CRES is the street-name abbreviation for crescent

explanation.surface: Fruit and bread rolls delivered to a house on a curved street.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British soft bread roll; place and crescent are abbreviated as they are on street signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab apples are small sour apples from wild or ornamental trees, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: French writer about river just after estuary

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the writer's name goes round what follows

blocks.note: André Gide was a French novelist
R is the abbreviation for river
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A French author writes about a river right after reaching its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estuary' sits at the end looking like part of the scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gironde is the large tidal estuary in south-west France where the Garonne and Dordogne meet.

clue.text: Video sent endlessly for broadcast showing steep plunge

indicators.note: without an end, so the word loses its final letter
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: Footage transmitted on air shows something falling sharply, such as share prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like transmission on air; it scatters VIDEO and SEN (SENT without its T).
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a sudden steep descent, of an aircraft or figuratively of prices.

clue.text: Refugee and actor once following road

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the actor's name is placed second, behind the road

blocks.note: the M1 motorway, written MI in crosswords
Cary Grant, the late film star

explanation.surface: A displaced person and a former film star travel down the highway together.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is someone who moves from their homeland, a near synonym for a person seeking refuge.

clue.text: Terminate, as it were, change in appearance

blocks.note: first meaning: to cause to be over, read literally
second meaning: a transformation of someone's look

explanation.walkthrough: 'As it were' warns that the first meaning is a playful literal reading: to render something finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the phrase is a noun for a restyling of hair, clothes or decor; split, it means to bring to an end.

clue.text: Car keys lost? Endless argument takes place in this sacred site

indicators.note: things that are lost are all over the place, so the letters are muddled
with no end, so the following word drops its last letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Tourists lose the hire car keys and start squabbling at a famous holy landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR KEYS plus RO (ROW cut short) are mixed together. The sacred site is the great sandstone monolith in central Australia, now called Uluru.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayers Rock is the huge red rock in the Northern Territory, held sacred by its Aboriginal owners.

clue.text: Rowing boat about to leave? It's an infallible indication

indicators.note: to leave means to depart, so the abbreviation for about goes away

blocks.note: a coracle is a small round boat paddled by one person
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A small boat is about to set off, which is a sure sign of something.
explanation.walkthrough: CORACLE without its C leaves ORACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a source of authoritative, supposedly unerring guidance or prophecy.

clue.text: Fuss in wake of advertising for gallery

indicators.note: in the wake of means coming behind, so the fuss is placed after the advertising

blocks.note: PR, public relations, is promotion
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: An uproar follows a publicity campaign for an art exhibition space.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado is the great national art museum in Madrid, an example of a gallery.

clue.text: Talk foolishly about institute operating illegally

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for foolish talk wraps round the abbreviation

blocks.note: to prate is to chatter idly
I is the abbreviation for institute

explanation.surface: Someone gossips about an organisation that is breaking the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a pirate radio station, it describes something unlicensed and unlawful.

clue.text: It's contracted in Yorkshire Dales

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A statement that something has been signed up or shrunk in a scenic northern English region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' tempts as shrunk; here it means taken on under contract. The Yorkshire Dales are upland valleys in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hired is to be engaged for payment, employed under an agreement.

clue.text: Noble disregarding bishop in party

indicators.note: disregarding means ignoring, so the letter for bishop is left out

blocks.note: brave can mean fine and noble, as in a brave new world
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An aristocrat at a celebration pays no attention to the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAVE without B leaves RAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large lively gathering with dance music, a kind of celebration or bash.

clue.text: Pay chap or otherwise get some unofficial books

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pay a man, or find some other way to acquire pirated volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are writings excluded from the accepted canon of the Bible, so they lack official standing.

clue.text: Old court star around four returns for comeback

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the tennis player wraps round the number
returning means going back the way it came, so the whole is read right to left

blocks.note: Rod Laver, the great Australian tennis champion of the 1960s
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A veteran tennis champion returns to the game at forty-something for a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Laver won the tennis Grand Slam twice; 'court' is the tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A revival is a return to prominence or popularity, which is what a comeback is.

clue.text: Greatest time with group in river

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the name of the river

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
R.E.M. was an American rock group
the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: The finest moment of a band's career spent by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means utmost or furthest in degree, the highest possible level.
